item.title: Why Organizations Take the Forms They Do — Coase, Jensen and Meckling, and Moe
item.description:
Vale and Mara introduce and discuss Coase (1937), Jensen and Meckling (1976), and Moe (1984). Separate chapters explain firm boundaries, ownership and financing incentives, and public bureaucracy before comparing their threads and tensions. Significant terms are defined for listeners new to the field. 43:51; five chapters. Independently authored whole-source readings and dialogue, with source fidelity review. Synthetic voices generated locally with Qwen and Kokoro. This is an explanatory discussion, not a verbatim reading.

Sources (APA)

  • Coase, R. H. (1937). The Nature of the Firm. Economica, 4(16), 386–405. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1468-0335.1937.tb00002.x
  • Jensen, M. C., & Meckling, W. H. (1976). Theory of the Firm: Managerial Behavior, Agency Costs and Ownership Structure. Journal of Financial Economics, 3(4), 305–360. https://doi.org/10.1016/0304-405X(76)90026-X
  • Moe, T. M. (1984). The New Economics of Organization. American Journal of Political Science, 28(4), 739–777. https://doi.org/10.2307/2110997

item.title: Does AI Assistance Enhance or Erode Expertise? — Mara’s oral adaptation
item.description:
Mara presents a source-grounded oral adaptation of the September 2026 NBER working paper on a three-month randomized experiment with patent lawyers. Covers the drafting and unaided redlining tasks, findings by experience, possible mechanisms, and limits of the evidence. 23:07; nine chapters. Synthetic narration generated locally with Kokoro Heart. This is an adaptation, not a verbatim reading. The source is a working paper, not peer reviewed.

Sources (APA)

  • Autor, D., Rodchenko, T., Martin, J., Iscenko, Z., Strand, S., Pearl, D., & Ferere, M. (2026). Does AI assistance enhance or erode expertise? Evidence from a three-month field experiment in patent drafting (NBER Working Paper No. 35720). National Bureau of Economic Research. https://doi.org/10.3386/w35720
